recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-8045 unless the work group separately reopens DetectedIssue severity policy, and any future change should account for FHIR-44528's preferred CodeableConcept decision.
issue_request: FHIR-8045 was a Published, Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 vocabulary issue for the former Alert/Contraindication area. It asked that ContraindicationSeverity stop using the v3 SeverityObservation H/M/L value set directly and instead use native FHIR high, moderate, and low codes, with mappings to v2/v3 where possible.
initial_application: Jira comments record SVN revisions 5731 and 5732. The relevant source application is git commit af86b5382c64c6172b7046bb2baf47422de44291 (SVN r5732), which changed the Contraindication severity example from H to high, changed the binding source from the v3 SeverityObservation value set to an internal #contraindication-severity list, changed the visible choices to high | moderate | low, and added v3 ObservationValue mappings for H, M, and L.
additional_context: Contraindication was renamed to DetectedIssue by #8043 in commit 1408563d743f15eff785f59063b34b538b4d4651. source/fhir.ini now records DetectedIssue as active and Contraindication as removed/renamed. A later Applied R6 issue, FHIR-44528, intentionally changed DetectedIssue.severity from required code to preferred CodeableConcept, so the current non-required binding is later work-group intent rather than a missed part of FHIR-8045.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current DetectedIssue CodeSystem and ValueSet define high, moderate, and low native codes, and the current ConceptMap maps those codes to v3 ObservationValue H, M, and L. Reverting the binding strength to required would conflict with FHIR-44528.

related_jiras.note: Applied R6 decision that intentionally changed DetectedIssue.severity to CodeableConcept with preferred binding, explaining why current source should not be restored to required.
Historical rename from Contraindication to DetectedIssue carries the old severity value set into the current build-scope successor resource.
